title: Ionic transferred-label bond
statement: An ionic bond is stable joint recurrence of opposed cation/anion held charge fibres produced by closed charge transfer, with electrostatic attraction and both chemical identities retained.
generation_rule: Generate the literal product of the registered ionic carrier, formation, orientation, interaction, identity, character, record and extension choices.
grammar_boundary: Every finite charge-transfer product containing opposed cation/anion held fibres whose closed electric interaction yields stable joint recurrence while both chemical identities remain retained.

choices.name: neutral-atom-pair-only
choices.reason: The ionic class requires retained ion carriers.

choices.name: unpaired-charge-creation
choices.reason: Charge cannot appear without conserved transfer.

choices.name: closed-charge-transfer
choices.reason: Every charge-state change is paired to a carrier path.

choices.name: opposed-held-charge-fibres
choices.reason: Cation and anion are structural orientations.

choices.name: generic-proximity
choices.reason: Proximity does not explain ionic stability.

choices.name: electrostatic-attraction-support
choices.reason: Opposed held electric labels generate reciprocal attraction.

choices.name: element-identity-erased
choices.reason: Ion formation preserves nuclear element identity.

choices.name: pure-binary-dogma
choices.reason: Observed bonds may retain both ionic and shared support.

choices.name: exact-support-composition
choices.reason: Ionic character is the exact retained share of charge-separated support.

choices.name: ionic-label-only
choices.reason: A label cannot reconstruct transfer and attraction.

choices.name: ion-transfer-interaction-trace
choices.reason: Formation, charges and recurrence remain held.

choices.name: free-electronegativity-cutoff
choices.reason: A fitted cutoff would import the classification.

choices.name: no-extra-rule
choices.reason: Charge separation and stable interaction determine the class.

induction_base: One closed charge transfer producing opposed retained ion fibres and stable reciprocal attraction supplies the first ionic bond.
induction_step: Appending one generated ion pair preserves charge conservation, atomic identities and all electrostatic interaction traces.
exclusions: no IUPAC bond definition, orbital equation, electronegativity scale, measured value or V2 answer may select a candidate
no numerical zero, negative, irrational, imaginary or floating proof quantity
no free, fitted, learned or target-derived parameter
no application result or opaque predictor
no universal bond-length/strength formula inferred from a categorical correspondence
official target content opens only through post-seal custody
Every finite charge-transfer product containing opposed cation/anion held fibres whose closed electric interaction yields stable joint recurrence while both chemical identities remain retained.
operational_witnesses: opposed cation/anion fibres retain reciprocal attraction
every charge state has a paired transfer
no electronegativity threshold selects the class
falsification_condition: The claim fails if IUPAC lacks cation/anion carriers, electrostatic attraction or the ionic-character boundary, or if a changed row is accepted.
